title: Canonical affine-base coherent reduced coproduct for abelian spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces with their small etale ringed sites [def-trf-algebraic-space] and the existing small affine etale models and restriction equivalences [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model]. For $X$ over $S$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$ on that model, set $H_X^n(M)=H^n(X_{et},M_{ab})$, using right derived global sections of its underlying additive sheaf. For a flat map $f:X\to Y$ [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], use the recorded tensor inverse image [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback]. Its cohomology pullback is the unique natural family $H_Y^n\to H_X^n f^*$ commuting with connecting maps of every module short exact sequence and in degree zero sending a global module section $s:\mathcal O_Y\to M$ to $f^*s$ via the normalized identification $f^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X$. This family exists uniquely. Let $T$ be a scheme over $S$ with an isomorphism $T\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R$ is a commutative ring. For $p:Y\to T$, $q:X\to T$ and $f:X\to Y$ with $pf=q$, use the scalar pullback $N_Y=\mathcal O_Y\otimes_RN$ of [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections]. There is a unique natural coefficient comparison $f^*N_Y\simeq N_X$ that sends each pulled-back global pure section $1\otimes n$ to $1\otimes n$. Combine it with flat cohomology pullback. Let $A$ have a natural commutative group structure [def-sfb-smooth-integral-group-space] and suppose its structural map is an abelian family as in [def-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-data]. Set $B=A\times_ST$, $C=B\times_TB$ using that node's actual fibre products, $p:B\to T$, $q:C\to T$, and $p_1,p_2:C\to B$. Define $m:C\to B$ by the universal property from the given addition on $A$ and the common projection to $T$. The identities $pm=q=pp_2$ hold (and $pp_1=q$ by definition); $m,p_1,p_2$ are flat. For every $R$-module $N$, define $D_{A,T,N}=m^*-p_1^*-p_2^*:H_B^2(N_B)\to H_C^2(N_C)$ by those actual flat pullbacks and normalized coefficient comparisons. No finiteness or flatness assumption on $N$ or Noetherian or reducedness assumption on $T$ is imposed.
